summary: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the Old Catholic Seminary of Amersfoort, the Sorbonne, and under Dasturs Darab and Kaus, later serving at the Bibliothèque nationale and Institut de France.

Abraham Richard Fuller was an Indology and history scholar and military officer. He served as a Lieutenant in the Bengal Army (1849), Major in the Royal Artillery, and Director of the Department of Public Instruction, Punjab (1860–1867).

Abraham Sachs was a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (circa 1934–1937) and held posts at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (circa 1953–1983).

Abraham Yohannan worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied under A. V. Williams Jackson at Columbia University (circa 1894–1898), where he subsequently held an academic post from circa 1894 to 1925.
Abraham Zablocki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under Anton Walter Florus Gueth, Mahasi Sayadaw, and U Nārada. He also taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, later holding posts at the University of Munich (2004–2006) and Hamburg (attested 2026).

Achyutananda Dash specializes in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University (attested 1999).

Ada Maryla Falk worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at the University of Florence and Sapienza University of Rome under Pavolini, Pettazzoni, Formichi, and Tucci. She taught Polish at the University of Calcutta and Polish and Sanskrit at Sapienza.

Adalbert Bezzenberger worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Göttingen and Munich under Theodor Benfey and Martin Haug, served as Privatdozent at Göttingen (1874), and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-European at the University of Königsberg (1879–1921).

Adalbert J. Gail was a scholar of Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Helmut Hoffmann (circa 1964–1968) and served as a professor at the Free University of Berlin (circa 1978–2006).

Adalbert Kuhn was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Louis Poley. He held teaching and directorial posts at Cöllnisches Gymnasium (1837–1870) and was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at La Trobe University (1997–2004) under Greg Bailey and became an Associate Professor at the University of Queensland in 2009.

Adam Hardy is an architectural historian and Indologist who studied architecture at the University of Cambridge. He held professorships at De Montfort University (circa 1993–2000) and Cardiff University (from 2004), and directed PRASADA.

Adam Heinz was a linguist who studied at the University of Lviv under Jerzy Kuryłowicz and Jagiellonian University under Jan Safarewicz. He taught at the Pedagogical University of Krakow and Jagiellonian University, becoming Professor of General Linguistics in 1973.
Adam Hohenberger was an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig (1913–1918) under the supervision of Ernst Windisch.

Adam Miller works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (2014–2022) and an MA at the University of Missouri, later holding adjunct instructor positions at Central Methodist, Western Illinois, Heartland, Towson, and Mercyhurst.

Adam Pearcey is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier. He founded and serves as Senior Editor and Translator for Lotsawa House.

Adam Yuet Chau is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Stanford University (1994–2001), held a fellowship at Harvard University, and became Professor of the Anthropology of China at the University of Cambridge in 2008.
Adele Schlombs is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who served at the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln from circa 1991 to 2022.
